chunks: From him, from Muhammad ibn Abi Umayr, from Hammad, from al-Halabi, who said:
Every oath that is not intended for the sake of Allah is of no effect, in divorce or otherwise.

key_terms.وَجْهُ اللَّهِ: The face of Allah (meaning for His sake/satisfaction)

ai.seo_question: What makes an Islamic oath legally binding or void?
ai.summary: Shaykh al-Tusi records this concise ruling in the chapter on oaths, emphasizing that the validity of a yamin hinges on the sincerity of the intention (niyyah) directed toward Allah. This principle ensures that oaths made for trivial or worldly gains lack legal force, a nuance particularly significant in Shia jurisprudence when determining the immediacy of divorce (talaq) or expiation (kaffarah).
